subject: Penetration test scope clarification — Hosted / Dedicated / Private (Acme Retail)
messages:
From: Jane Li <security@acme-retail.com>
To: sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com
Cc: security_ops@acme-retail.com
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: penetration test report + scope questions

Hi Sergio,

We're updating our vendor risk file for Q1 and need to confirm the scope of Redwood's most recent penetration test and the remediation status for a couple of previously reported findings. Specifically:

- Which deployment types are covered by your external pen test report: Hosted API (shared multi-tenant), Redwood Dedicated (Redwood-managed dedicated GPU pools), Private/VPC (customer-managed VPC with Redwood control plane), and fully on-prem installations?
- For Dedicated deployments, do tests include the reserved GPU pool host environment and any shared control-plane components that manage the pool?
- Do you include managed services that touch customer data (KMS integrations, telemetry collectors, object storage endpoints) in scope?

Please attach the latest pen test report or provide a SOC-equivalent summary and a matrix mapping included/excluded components. We also have two prior findings on record (open S3 ACL and outdated nginx package) — can you confirm remediation status or mitigations?

I've attached our questionnaire to help align scope: [Attachment: acme_pen_test_questions.xlsx (xlsx)].

Thanks,
Jane Li
Senior Information Security Analyst
Acme Retail
[Attachment: acme_pen_test_questions.xlsx]

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jane Li <security@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: penetration test report + scope questions

Hi Jane — thanks for the clear list. Short answer up front: our external penetration test (latest report attached) covers our Redwood-managed control plane, hosted public endpoints, and Redwood-managed Dedicated pools; it does not cover customer-managed on-prem networks or the portions of Private deployments that are fully customer-controlled (for example, if the customer runs their own gateway or storage inside a VPC we do not run external network scans inside their VPC).

High-level scope mapping (attached as a matrix):
- Hosted API: included (public endpoints, ingress layers, authentication flows, runtime service nodes managed by Redwood)
- Dedicated (Redwood-managed): included (host OS for GPU hosts, orchestration nodes we operate, shared control-plane components)
- Private / VPC: mixed — Redwood-managed control plane components are included; customer-managed workload inside a private VPC is out of scope unless we have explicit testing access arranged.
- On-prem (customer-installed packages): out of scope unless we run a dedicated engagement on-site or via customer-provided access.

I've attached a scope matrix that maps components (API gateway, runtime, KV caches, telemetry, KMS integrations, object storage endpoints) to included/excluded and noted the typical evidence we can provide (scan outputs, remediation tickets, architecture diagrams).

Two quick asks:
1) Can you confirm which deployment(s) Acme runs in production (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC vs on-prem)? You mentioned Hosted earlier but double-checking.
2) Do you need a whitebox or blackbox engagement for Dedicated pools? We normally provide the external pen test report (blackbox) plus host/hardening evidence for Dedicated.

Attachments: redwood_pen_test_scope_matrix.xlsx

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Security & Compliance Liaison
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_pen_test_scope_matrix.xlsx]

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jane Li <security@acme-retail.com>, sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: penetration test report + scope questions

Hi Jane — adding some technical detail to Sergio's helpful summary so you can map to your questionnaire items:

What we include in our standard external pen test (most recent report attached):
- Public ingress points for Hosted API (load balancers, TLS termination, oauth flows).
- Redwood-managed Dedicated: external-facing orchestration endpoints and the host OS of the GPU nodes we operate (we do not run tests inside customer-controlled VPC networks).
- KMS integrations: we test the interaction patterns (API auth, key-access flows) but we do not have access to customer-managed KMS keys; we can provide logs and config evidence for the integration.
- Object storage: external endpoints we control are tested; for customer-managed buckets (inside a VPC or under the customer's AWS account) those are outside of our scope.
- Caching/Redis: if hosted/managed by Redwood, the service endpoints are included in external testing; if customers bring their own caching inside private networks, it's excluded.

Included artifacts we can share under an NDA: external pentest report (redacted), host hardening checklists, remediation ticket links, and a remediation summary table. We typically redact IPs for shared environments.

Quick note on the two findings you referenced:
- Open S3 ACL: that was a misconfiguration in a customer onboarding project in 2025 — it was remediated in Oct 2025 and we have the Jira remediation ticket (JIRA-SEC-1942) and verification scan.
- Outdated nginx: an agent-level package on a legacy build was upgraded and a patching cadence has been added; verification included in the 2025Q4 pen test appendix.

Attaching: pen_test_report_redwood_2025Q4.pdf (redacted) and internal verification artifacts. Happy to walk through specific questionnaire rows on a call.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Senior Infra/Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pen_test_report_redwood_2025Q4.pdf]

- A Dedicated pool (dedicated-redwood-01) used for payment-related inference (we consider that high-sensitivity)

Requesting the following so we can close out the vendor risk item:
1) Please confirm Dedicated pool (dedicated-redwood-01) host-level testing is included in your external pen test scope and provide the remediation summary for any high/critical findings in the last test.
2) Please confirm managed Redis/cache endpoints owned by Redwood are included in the external test scope (we use those in payments flow).
3) If any components are out of scope (for example customer-managed VPC buckets), please list them explicitly in the scope matrix so our risk team can accept residual risk or request a targeted assessment.

We also need confirmation of timelines for remediation documentation (Jira links or PRs) for the two prior findings. If possible, we'd like a short 30-minute call early next week to walk these items with your security and infra leads.

Vendor risk portal link: https://vendor-risk.acme-retail.com/requests/4281

Jane Li
